players.product: PCIe / CXL retimers and high-speed interface ICs

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 consolidated revenue was $134.48 million, up 6.61% sequentially and 0.73% year-over-year (vs $133.50 million a year ago); net income $18.78 million (vs $22.79 million), EPS $0.24 (vs $0.29); gross profit $54.06 million, up 6.35% from the previous quarter and down 6.06% year-over-year. CEO: revenue mix DP 30%, high speed (PS) about 45%, TC slightly above 10%, TT (incl. the TTED device) slightly below 15%; TT grew faster than expected on many notebook model wins.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $134.48 million (+6.61% QoQ, +0.73% YoY); net income $18.78 million; EPS $0.24; gross profit $54.06 million; mix DP 30% / high speed 45% / TC above 10% / TT below 15%

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 guidance: revenue between $139 million-$153 million, gross margin 40%-44%, operating expense $33 million-$36 million. CEO: Q3 is the traditional notebook hot season and TT/TTED will keep growing as a share; margin should slightly improve in Q3 and he hopes Q2 gross margin bottomed. Full year: the early-2026 view was more positive, but high DRAM and storage prices suppressed notebook demand (gaming notebooks down a lot); Parade hopes Q4 can be a few percentage points above last year, Q4 PO receiving looks good but it does not want to commit too early; Q4 should follow largely normal seasonality.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $139 million-$153 million; GM 40%-44%; opex $33 million-$36 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: OSAT (back-end) prices rose suddenly and multiple times in the quarter. Parade is responding two ways: price increases passed to customers selectively, segment by segment (some already in place, others being negotiated this quarter, most customers willing to take some adjustment), and moving to cheaper back-end suppliers and lower-cost foundries, since many customers do not require UMC or TSMC (e.g. mature TTED devices). Foundry price increases talked about for 2027 are not included in guidance.

CEO on the ASIC-like custom-chip project: two big, complicated devices developed with the customer (system design, FPGA/emulation and software work done jointly); the first chip tapes out later this quarter (Q3 2026) and the second quickly after; revenue contribution expected in the later part (second half) of 2027. Single-device price in the $10, $20 range; gross margin expected in the neighborhood of the corporate margin, depending on yield.
quarterly_data.figure: first tape-out later Q3 2026; revenue 2H 2027; device price $10-$20 range

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on TTED (integrated T-Con, source driver and touch for notebook panels): Parade had expected above 5 million units this year and shipments are now much higher; one device per notebook panel, replacing two or three source drivers, one T-Con and one or two touch chips and removing the T-Con board. New devices address oxide panels and a high-end TTED with 120 Hz refresh, touch and active stylus, developed with Wacom. Reaching 10% to 11% of total notebooks is seen as quite reachable; he has not seen competition so far. Integrated-solution margin is approaching the corporate margin.
quarterly_data.figure: above 5 million units 2026 (now much higher); 10%-11% notebook share target

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on data center: Parade continues to ship PCIe Gen 5 and Gen 4 retimers for data-center storage plus redrivers on motherboards; first-half 2026 data-center revenue was about equivalent to 2025, excluding cables. Using the silicon germanium cable-driver assets acquired from Spectra7 last year (112G and 224G), a customer built a 1.6T Ethernet ACC cable (3-5 meter class) that tested well at the Plugfest in New Hampshire; PCIe Gen 6 cables are being worked on with a leading server customer. Two to four Parade ICs per cable depending on design; the cable customer has not yet given a clear mass-production time.
quarterly_data.figure: 112G and 224G cable drivers; 1.6T Ethernet cable; 2 to 4 ICs per cable

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on PCs: 2026 notebook units are widely believed to be down about 10% after the DRAM price increase and the CPU shortage in Q1-Q2; AMD and Intel CPU supply is no longer an issue, NVIDIA and Qualcomm are joining the notebook CPU segment and NVIDIA systems start shipping later in Q3, where Parade has two or more associated devices. He keeps a positive view for 2027 on AI edge computing demand. Other long-term (Standard-plus) customers remain healthy and less hit by DRAM; several chips developed with them start production in later 2027 or 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 notebook units ~10% reduction (industry view cited by CEO)
